domains.MB: Many-body state spaces, fermionic and bosonic degrees of freedom, operators and state representations used by the scientific engine.
domains.SOL: Numerical methods that turn Hamiltonians and operators into eigenstates, low-energy manifolds, response functions and converged results.
domains.PHY: Physical Hamiltonian terms and experimental geometry needed to model atomic, ligand-field and cluster physics.
domains.SPEC: Spectroscopic observables and response-function machinery for X-ray and photoemission-style experiments.
domains.MAT: Cluster, tight-binding and material-facing models that bridge local many-body physics to realistic electronic-structure input.
domains.DYN: Density-matrix, mean-field and time-evolution capabilities for static and dynamical many-body states.
domains.RUN: Typed runtime contracts, execution backends, reproducibility controls and simulation context.
domains.VAL: Independent Quanty execution, parity evidence, convergence and semantic cross-validation.
domains.UX: Interfaces through which users configure, run, inspect and integrate XMD Quantum calculations.

MB1.summary: Constructs fermionic Fock-space basis states from occupation-number configurations.

MB2.summary: Restricts the determinant space to physically relevant sectors such as fixed particle number or bounded configurations.

MB3.summary: Implements creation and annihilation operators with fermionic anticommutation semantics.

MB4.summary: Represents quantum states and amplitudes in a form that can be transformed, solved and measured.

MB5.summary: Builds operator expressions and converts them to matrix or matrix-free actions over the chosen basis.

MB6.summary: Provides generic expectation-value and bra-ket semantics across supported state and operator types.

MB7.summary: Extends the state space with bosonic degrees of freedom such as vibrational or photon-like modes.

S1.summary: Solves bounded Hamiltonians by dense diagonalization when the complete matrix is practical.

S2.summary: Uses Krylov/Lanczos subspaces to obtain extremal states and response information without forming the full dense matrix.

S3.summary: Targets the low-energy part of the spectrum needed for ground-state and finite-temperature calculations.

S4.summary: Defines complete ensemble semantics for weighted mixtures of states and observables.

S5.summary: Controls numerical stopping criteria and evidence that a computed result is stable against solver settings.

S6.summary: Moves Krylov-style numerical kernels to GPU execution while preserving numerical and scientific acceptance contracts.

P1.summary: Models atomic multiplet structure arising from electron-electron interactions and angular-momentum coupling.

P2.summary: Represents electron-electron Coulomb interactions using Slater-integral parameterizations.

P3.summary: Adds spin-orbit coupling to the Hamiltonian.

P4.summary: Represents general crystal-field terms beyond a single hard-coded symmetry.

P5.summary: Defines arbitrary beam, field and sample orientations through explicit geometry rather than fixed axes.

P6.summary: Constructs transition operators for linear, circular and general polarization states.

P7.summary: Includes ligand-to-metal charge-transfer configurations and their coupling to local states.

P8.summary: Extends the local model to cluster/Anderson-style impurity Hamiltonians with bath or ligand degrees of freedom.

X1.summary: Computes X-ray absorption from dipole-allowed transitions into final states.

X2.summary: Computes linear dichroism as the polarization-dependent difference between absorption spectra.

X3.summary: Computes magnetic circular dichroism from left- and right-circularly polarized absorption.

X4.summary: Weights initial states with a thermal ensemble before evaluating observables.

X5.summary: Applies physical/instrumental broadening and energy resolution to discrete spectral lines.

X6.summary: Evaluates Green's functions and continued-fraction response representations.

X7.summary: RIXS describes a second-order resonant scattering process with an intermediate core-excited state.

X8.summary: Photoemission and inverse-photoemission probe electron removal and addition spectral weight.

X9.summary: XES/nIXS cover emission and non-resonant inelastic scattering response channels.

X10.summary: Fluorescence yield integrates selected radiative decay channels after excitation.

X11.summary: Provides a reusable abstraction for frequency-dependent response calculations.

M1.summary: A bounded cluster reference model used as a controlled parity and regression target.

M2.summary: Generalizes cluster Hamiltonians beyond the bounded reference case.

M3.summary: Defines a typed tight-binding model for lattice orbitals, hoppings and onsite terms.

M4.summary: Supports finite/open and periodic cluster boundary conditions.

M5.summary: Ingests electronic-structure information from DFT/Wannier-style sources into model parameters.

M6.summary: Represents frequency-dependent hybridization between an interacting subsystem and its environment.

D1.summary: Represents mixed quantum states through a density matrix.

D2.summary: Constructs a density matrix from states, ensembles or solver output and exposes it to observables.

D3.summary: Builds effective mean-field operators from expectation values of interacting terms.

D4.summary: Finds a self-consistent mean-field ground state.

D5.summary: Evolves a ground state under an explicitly time-dependent Hamiltonian.

D6.summary: Provides general unitary or density-matrix time evolution.

R5.summary: Maps typed native XMD models to independent Quanty execution while failing closed when semantics cannot be represented safely.

R9.summary: Defines explicit simulation conditions such as temperature, field, polarization, geometry, pressure and resolution. Presets resolve to concrete values rather than ambiguous labels.

V2.summary: Compares bounded atomic XMD results with independently executed Quanty references under explicit tolerances.

V3.summary: Extends parity evidence to finite-temperature populations and spectra.

V5.summary: Compares cluster-model energies, strengths and spectra against Quanty reference execution.

V7.summary: Automates cross-validation so scientific differences are detected and surfaced during CI/evidence generation.

V9.summary: Verifies immutable evidence, discovers new evidence families and derives sanitized statistics/dashboards without assigning unsupported semantics to unknown families.
